- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) or shows strong bearish momentum, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–4% to align with mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns from neutral to bullish; add 1–2 days of delay in forecast adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-period moving average) to reduce noise-driven overreactions.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 7-day mean as anchor.
